messages:
maria: heads-up: saw a big jump in evictions in us-west1 around 21:10 UTC — mixed pools (gpu-preempt + on-demand) lost ~18% spot capacity, tail latency spiked for streaming requests. thinking we should try a rate-aware requeue + token-stream cutover to on-demand rather than immediate full failover. thoughts?
liam: +1 to rate-aware. immediate full failover burns on-demand and spikes cost. do we have per-host requeue counters to avoid stampedes?
jordan: we emit `requeue_attempts` per worker but it's per-request not per-host. we can add a sliding-window counter on the worker agent to limit requeues to N/s. simple token bucket.
maria: exactly — proposal: when eviction/soft-drain observed, start a 2s token-stream cutover window where in-flight streaming connections swap tokens to a fallback queue. within that window, each worker allows up to 30 requeues/s (burst 60) before handing off to on-demand capacity.
sanjay: +1 but need to be careful about QoS: some requests are latency-sensitive. can we classify routes and allow higher requeue rate for non-interactive batch ones?
liam: route-aware thresholds make sense. we should also exponential-backoff requeue attempts per-request and cap at 3 attempts. avoid retry storms.
jordan: rough config sketch (agent policy):

```yaml
requeue_policy:
  sliding_window_ms: 2000
  per_worker_rate: 30
  per_route_multiplier:
    low_priority: 0.5
    default: 1.0
    critical: 2.0
  max_requeues_per_request: 3
  token_cutover_grace_ms: 1500
  fallback_strategy: on_demand_pool
```

maria: also include a short "soft drain" state: worker enters SOFT_DRAIN when preempt warning received; during SOFT_DRAIN it rejects new allocations but accepts requeues up to window. after SOFT_DRAIN timeout it moves to DRAIN and streams token cutover completes.
liam: how about metrics & alerts? we need new graphs: requeue_rate, per_worker_requeue_throttle, requeue_to_on_demand_ratio, and cost_delta estimate when fallback triggers.
sanjay: we should gate fallback by a budget: per-epoch on-demand spend cap so we don't accidentally blow monthly commit. fallback only allowed if fallback_cost < budget_remaining * 0.05 (for example). add a kill-switch for account teams.
maria: good call. add a quick pseudo-alert for >5% of requests hitting fallback for >3m.
infra-bot: alert: cluster/us-west1 preemptible_loss spike at 2148529600, affected_nodes=172, estimated_fallback_cost/hr=2.3k USD.
jordan: infra-bot numbers check out. question: how do we do token streaming cutover for long-lived streams? we need a small protocol change: stream should carry a resumable token id + resume_offset. workers can push a brief resume token to the client and client retries to fallback endpoint with token.
liam: implement server-side proxy that accepts resume token and patches KV cache prefix to continue. fallback endpoint must mount same model version and kv namespace mapping. risk: cache warmup cost. maybe we allow best-effort warm cache fetch via async prefetch during cutover window.
maria: add a lightweight gradation: 1) allow requeue within window (cheap), 2) if throttled -> issue resume token and async prefetch, 3) if resume fails after 3s -> force on-demand direct fallback and charge cost.
sanjay: can we simulate this in a canary? run on 5% of traffic from low-priority routes in us-west1 for 24h and compare cost + tail p95. we need to ensure SLOs.
jordan: i'll spin a canary: agent build + config toggle `rate_requeue_v2` targeting 5% low-priority routes. will post deployment ts.
maria: thanks. one more: update routing policy to prefer regional on-demand before cross-region fallback to avoid network egress and added latency.
liam: agree. and add a metric that tracks cross-region fallback count.
maria: action items:
- jordan: create agent PR + canary config (due EOD PST)
- liam: add Grafana panels + alerts (due tomorrow)
- sanjay: propose fallback budget formula and add kill-switch (due tomorrow)
- infra: monitor canary and post results in this thread

maria: ping @jordan when PR ready, i'll run a quick review. :thumbsup:
jordan: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/agent/pulls/8421 (canary flag `rate_requeue_v2`). deployment started at 2148529710.
liam: dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/d/evict/requeue-rates (added panels, alerting rule `evict.requeue.fallback_ratio > 0.05 for 3m`).
sanjay: budget PR in flight: https://git.internal/redwood/costs/pulls/328 (adds per-cluster fallback cap).
maria: perfect. we'll iterate after 24h canary. thanks all.
